definition: Rockmelt was a Chromium-based web browser designed to integrate social-network and content-sharing functions into browsing.
example: A software historian compares how Rockmelt displayed social updates alongside a web page.
sense_note: Discontinued historical product; brand was also used for a later content-discovery product.

definition: FactoryTalk is Rockwell Automation's family of industrial software for functions such as visualization, data collection, and production operations.
example: A plant uses FactoryTalk View to display machine status and alarms to operators.

definition: Role-based access control assigns permissions to roles and grants access to users through their assigned roles.
example: A payroll system lets people in the payroll approver role authorize a payment while other users can only review it.

definition: Roof bolting stabilizes the rock above an underground opening by anchoring and reinforcing it with installed bolts.
example: A mine safety engineer reviews a support plan for an underground passage before workers enter it.

definition: Route management plans, monitors, and adjusts routes to meet delivery or service commitments under constraints such as time, capacity, and access.
example: A dispatcher reassigns two deliveries when a road closure puts one truck behind schedule.
sense_note: Likely transport sense; routing in networks or software is also possible.

definition: Routing Table Maintenance Protocol is an AppleTalk distance-vector routing protocol that exchanges reachability information to maintain network routes.
example: A network historian interprets an archived AppleTalk routing table using its reported hop counts.

definition: RSA Archer is enterprise software for governance, risk, and compliance workflows, including risk assessments, control tracking, and audit documentation.
example: A compliance team links a control test to its evidence and assigns a remediation owner in Archer.
sense_note: Legacy brand; verify product naming as needed.

definition: Rx30 is pharmacy management software for processing prescriptions and supporting workflow such as claims, inventory, and dispensing records.
example: A community pharmacy uses Rx30 to reconcile the inventory associated with dispensed prescriptions.

definition: RxKotlin adds Kotlin-friendly extensions and utilities for composing reactive streams with RxJava.
example: A developer uses an extension to combine the latest readings from two observable data streams.

definition: The Safe Drinking Water Act is the U.S. federal law authorizing protections for public drinking water, including standards, oversight, and monitoring requirements.
example: A public water utility uses applicable standards to plan its sampling and reporting.

definition: Safety audits systematically check practices, records, and conditions against safety requirements to identify gaps and corrective actions.
example: An auditor reviews training records and observes equipment use before documenting areas for correction.

definition: Sage Intacct is cloud financial management software for accounting and reporting functions such as the general ledger, payables, and receivables.
example: A nonprofit generates a statement that breaks expenses out by program.

definition: Sage MAS 90 is a legacy business management system for accounting, inventory, and operational workflows that became part of the Sage 100 product line.
example: A migration specialist maps accounts from a MAS 90 ledger to a replacement system.
sense_note: Legacy brand; verify exact edition when relevant.

definition: Sailing instruction teaches learners to handle a sailboat, interpret conditions, maneuver, and follow safety practices.
example: An instructor has students practice tacking on a marked course while observing boat traffic.

definition: SailPoint IdentityIQ is identity governance software for administering access policies, reviewing entitlements, and supporting provisioning workflows.
example: A manager uses an access certification campaign to remove entitlements that staff no longer need.

definition: Sails.js is a Node.js web application framework with conventions for organizing models, controllers, and interfaces.
example: A developer creates a service for viewing and updating appointment records.

definition: Sales and operations planning is a recurring cross-functional process that aligns expected demand, operational capacity, inventory, and financial plans.
example: Sales and production teams agree on a feasible volume forecast before materials are ordered.

definition: A sales presentation explains an offering's fit and evidence to a prospective buyer and addresses objections or decision criteria.
example: A presenter shows how software would shorten a prospect's actual invoicing workflow.

definition: Salesforce Datorama is a marketing analytics platform for combining data across channels and reporting campaign performance, later branded Marketing Cloud Intelligence.
example: An analyst brings paid search and email campaign costs into one reporting dashboard.

definition: Salesforce Social Studio was a social media management application for publishing, listening, and engaging across connected channels.
example: A marketing analyst reviewing historical records checks how brand mentions were categorized in Social Studio.

definition: Salesforce is a cloud enterprise software platform and product family used to manage customer relationships and related workflows.
example: A sales team records customer interactions and tracks opportunities through defined stages.
sense_note: The label may denote the vendor, the overall platform, or a particular product.

definition: SAP Adaptive Server Enterprise is a relational database management system historically known as Sybase ASE and designed for transactional workloads.
example: An administrator monitors a transaction database and schedules backups under its recovery plan.

definition: SAP BusinessObjects is a business intelligence suite for querying organizational data and producing managed reports and dashboards.
example: A financial analyst builds a scheduled report of regional sales for department managers.

definition: SAP Crystal Reports is a reporting application for designing formatted reports from databases and other structured data sources.
example: A developer lays out a printable inventory report grouped by stockroom.

definition: SAP Fiori is SAP's design system and application experience for role-oriented business tasks across devices.
example: A purchasing clerk uses a Fiori app to view and act on assigned purchase approvals.

definition: SAP GUI is SAP's client interface for accessing classic SAP transactions and applications.
example: A warehouse clerk uses SAP GUI to display a material document by its number.

definition: SAP IoT refers to SAP technologies for connecting devices, collecting their measurements, and integrating device events with enterprise workflows.
example: A manufacturer uses equipment temperature readings to inform a maintenance workflow.
sense_note: Product names and offerings have changed; verify the intended edition.

definition: SAP IS-Retail is SAP's industry solution for retail processes such as assortment planning, merchandising, purchasing, and store inventory.
example: A retailer manages which products are available in each store's assortment.

definition: SAP Lumira is SAP software for creating interactive data visualizations and analytical applications.
example: An analyst builds an interactive view that lets managers compare sales across product lines.

definition: SAP Materials Management supports procurement and inventory processes, including purchasing, goods movement, and material records.
example: A buyer creates a purchase order and later checks whether the goods receipt matches it.

definition: SAP NetWeaver Process Integration is middleware for routing and transforming messages between SAP and other enterprise systems.
example: An integration developer maps purchase-order fields between two applications using different formats.

definition: SAP Quality Management is SAP functionality for planning inspections, recording quality results, and handling nonconformities in business processes.
example: A receiving team records an inspection and withholds a batch that fails an acceptance check.

definition: SAP S/4HANA is an enterprise resource planning suite built on the SAP HANA database for processes such as finance, procurement, production, and sales.
example: A manufacturer links a production order, material movements, and accounting postings in the same ERP suite.

definition: SAP Sovereign Cloud denotes SAP deployment offerings designed to satisfy jurisdiction-specific requirements for data location, operations, or control.
example: A public-sector team checks whether a proposed SAP deployment meets its contractual data and operator-location requirements.
sense_note: Offerings vary by country; the label does not establish compliance with any particular regime.

definition: SAP technology consulting helps organizations design, configure, integrate, migrate, and operate SAP systems against business requirements.
example: A consultant evaluates which existing interfaces must change during a migration to a new SAP environment.

definition: SAP refers to an enterprise software vendor or its broad ecosystem of applications and platforms for managing business processes.
example: An implementation team integrates purchasing and accounting using SAP software.
sense_note: The label does not identify a particular product or module.

definition: Savon is a Ruby library for using web services that expose a SOAP interface.
example: A Ruby application uses Savon to send a structured request to a legacy order service.
sense_note: Interpreted as the Ruby library based on the technical label.

definition: Scaffold building is the erection, alteration, or dismantling of temporary structures that support elevated work and access.
example: A qualified crew assembles a scaffold for façade work and has it inspected before use.
sense_note: Likely construction sense; software and instructional uses are possible.

definition: Scala.js compiles Scala programs to JavaScript so they can run in environments such as web browsers.
example: A developer compiles Scala code for an interactive chart that runs in a browser.

definition: Scalding is a Scala library for expressing distributed data processing jobs on infrastructure such as Hadoop, built on Cascading.
example: A data engineer defines a batch job that groups records by category and sums their values.
sense_note: Interpreted as the Scala library, not the thermal injury or processing technique.
